On 27 August 2017 at 01:52, sschnug <notifications@github.com> wrote:

> Description
>
> Reading this SO-issue
> <https://stackoverflow.com/questions/45896410/gaussiannb-valueerror-the-sum-of-the-priors-should-be-1/45897071#45897071>
> lead me to check the code in naive_bayes.py
> <https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/blob/ef5cb84a/sklearn/naive_bayes.py#L363>
> where the priors are checked.
>
> I did not check the whole method and what is internally assumed about
> these priors, but:
>
> if priors.sum() != 1.0:
>     raise ValueError('The sum of the priors should be 1.')
>
> obviously calls for trouble, like in the example in the above SO-post.
>
> import numpy as np
> priors = np.array([0.08, 0.14, 0.03, 0.16, 0.11, 0.16, 0.07, 0.14, 0.11, 0.0])
> my_sum = np.sum(priors)
> print('my_sum: ', my_sum)
> print('naive: ', my_sum == 1.0)
> print('safe: ', np.isclose(my_sum, 1.0))
>
> #('my_sum: ', 1.0000000000000002)
> #('naive: ', False)
> #('safe: ', True)
>
> Steps/Code to Reproduce
>
> Just take the official GaussianNB example
> <http://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.naive_bayes.GaussianNB.html>
> and use the numbers above.
> Expected Results
>
> Safe fp-math comparison OR internal correction when input-sum is expected
> to be close to 1.
> Actual Results
>
> ValueError('The sum of the priors should be 1.')
>
> Versions
>
> Current master.

Not as far as I can tell. You're welcome to have a go.

And maybe look at [this approach in discriminant analysis](https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/blob/5c6cc88967055c4845197c441bfe9751687359c4/sklearn/discriminant_analysis.py#L440) as potential fix.

        if (self.priors_ < 0).any():
            raise ValueError("priors must be non-negative")
        if self.priors_.sum() != 1:
            warnings.warn("The priors do not sum to 1. Renormalizing",
                          UserWarning)
            self.priors_ = self.priors_ / self.priors_.sum()

Maybe one could argue about making the <0 check more safe too (maybe relevant in complex pipeline), but i'm not sure if that's really needed.

Also: i highly recommend a simple/regex-like search for patterns like this in the whole repo, starting with ```== 1.0``` and ```!= 1.0```.

**EDIT:** As expected, the approach of normalizing like in ```discriminant_analysis.py``` also might fail to provide an array summing up to 1.0:

      __CPROVER_assume(b >= 0.0 and b <= 1.0 and isfinite(b));
      __CPROVER_assume(c >= 0.0 and c <= 1.0 and isfinite(c));
      // make it more interesting

      double a_ = a / sum;
      double b_ = b / sum;
      double c_ = c / sum;

      __CPROVER_assert( (a_ + b_ + c_) == 1., "Add up to 1?");

      return 1;
    }
